title: Error facade + retry-guard decorators and stream-resume ergonomics for SDKs
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: SDK consumers face inconsistent error types and opaque retry behavior across Python/TS/Go. Streaming interruptions are hard to resume because SDKs surface raw transport errors without a stable resume token protocol. This ticket proposes a small, language-idiomatic facade layer plus a lightweight retry-guard decorator and a standard resume-token handshake for streaming endpoints.
background: We have multiple tickets and PRs addressing error catalogs and retry ergonomics, but the UX for developers still varies by language. Customers see a mix of HTTP/transport exceptions, runtime panics, and SDK-specific wrappers with different metadata fields. Streaming clients lose useful progress context. A compact cross-language pattern will reduce friction while keeping implementation simple per-language.
proposal: Introduce an 'Error Facade' layer inside each SDK that exports a small, stable set of error classes: TransientError, PermanentError, QuotaError, AuthError, ValidationError, StreamInterrupted. Each class carries: code (string), message (string), retry_after (optional ISO timestamp), hint (optional user-facing action).

Add a language-native retry-guard decorator/wrapper (e.g., @retry_guard in Python, withRetryGuard(fn, opts) in TS, RetryGuard(func) in Go) that: applies exponential backoff with Jitter, consults error.code to decide retryability, reads retry_after, and emits telemetry hooks (beforeRetry, finalFailure).

Standardize streaming resume: server includes a resume_token in stream checkpoints (JSON metadata messages). On StreamInterrupted errors, SDK exposes resume_token via StreamInterrupted.error_metadata and offers a resume_stream(token, opts) helper that resumes from server-side cursor. If server lacks token, SDK surfaces a clear non-resumable error with suggested fallback (restart request with short prefix).
Surface actionable hints in error.hint (string) with one-sentence next steps, and provide an SDK utility translate_error_to_user_action(err) that returns concise guidance for UIs and support teams.

Ship small ergonomic wrappers and examples per language rather than changing the raw transport layer: keep underlying HTTP/WebSocket clients but map/augment their errors through the facade at boundary points.

Add comprehensive examples and tests: deterministic unit tests for mapping, integration tests that assert resume flows with synthetic checkpoint messages, and end-to-end fuzz tests for retry policy convergence.
acceptance_criteria: Each SDK exposes the new small error class set and maps existing error cases to those classes with a documented code string format (e.g., "ERR_TRANSIENT.KV_TIMEOUT").
Retry-guard decorator exists in Python/TS/Go with matching public signatures and tests demonstrating backoff + respect for retry_after headers.
Streaming endpoints include resume_token metadata in synthetic integration tests and SDK resume_stream(token) successfully resumes in >90% of simulated interruptions.
Docs and two end-user examples (chat and embeddings batch) updated to show how to handle StreamInterrupted and use translate_error_to_user_action.
Telemetry hooks implemented: beforeRetry, onRetryExhausted, onResumeAttempt; basic dashboards wired in staging to validate signals.
Design doc and API surface reviewed by SDK leads and Runtime team and design signoff recorded in comments.
rollback_criteria: If mapping causes large client breakages or >0.5% user-facing regressions in canary usage, revert facade mapping per language and revert to opt-in mode while we patch mappings. We'll monitor via canary error counts and a consumer feedback Slack channel set up in rollout plan.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement facade and retry-guard behind an opt-in flag in all SDKs. 2) Publish alpha SDKs to npm/pypi/goreleaser with docs linked. 3) Run a 1-week canary with a subset of internal customers and Redwood examples. 4) Flip opt-in to default after zero-severity block issues for 72 hours. 5) Announce migration path and deprecation schedule for old error shapes.
migration_notes: Provide a lightweight compatibility adapter: legacy_error -> ErrorFacade.map_legacy(err) which preserves original error.raw for debugging. Create a CLI script that scans codebase for exception classes and advises migration steps. Post-migration, keep legacy adapter for 6 months before removal.
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping coverage >95% for mapped scenarios, integration tests that simulate network interruptions and validate resume semantics, and canary with prod-like traffic for 72 hours recording error counts and resume success. Add fuzzer that replays malformed metadata to ensure graceful non-resumable behavior.
